Jordan — thanks, and welcome. Quick answers + attachments below.

Summary checklist (vendor preconditions)
- Signed vendor intake / W-9 (US) or W-8 / VAT certificate (EU) where applicable
- Legal business name, tax ID, and corporate address
- Bank remittance details (ACH/Wire + payee name) and payee contact for invoices
- Primary invoicing email and AP contact
- Entity validation (business registration or DUNS if available)
- Security questionnaire (if requested by our InfoSec team) — optional for basic onboarding, required for production access

PO issuance timing (typical)
- Vendor packet received & validated: 1–3 business days
- Finance/Procurement review & vendor creation: 2–5 business days
- Standard PO issuance after vendor created: 2–3 business days
- Typical end-to-end: ~5–10 business days from complete packet
- Urgent path: mark the intake as "expedite" and loop Dev (dev_patel) for SLA exception (can reduce to 48–72 hours in some cases)

Line-item formatting guidance (attached template: po_lineitem_template.csv)
- Required columns: description, sku_or_task_id, unit_of_measure, quantity, unit_price, currency, total_amount, start_date (if subscription), end_date (if term), gl_code (optional), cost_center (optional)
- Use one row per discrete billing item (do not combine subscription + one-time services in the same row)
- For subscriptions: include a separate row for recurring base fee and rows for any add-ons or usage tiers
- For SOWs: break into task-level rows with clear task IDs that map to the SOW appendix

Attachments included: redwood_vendor_intake_form_v1.pdf, po_lineitem_template.csv

Next steps (mutual action plan)
1) You return the vendor intake + W-9 (or VAT) and completed CSV sample
2) We validate and create the vendor record (1–3 business days)
3) Procurement issues PO once vendor exists (2–3 business days)

If the onboarding credit timeline is tight, propose a call with Dev for expedite — looping Dev Patel now.

Thanks —

Jordan — quick clarifications from finance on best practice for mapping: 

On Mon, May 3, 2027 at 09:10 Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Two examples to illustrate how to split lines so our AP system consumes them cleanly:
> 
> Example A — Subscription: 
> 1) description: "Redwood Hosted API — Standard (monthly)"; sku_or_task_id: "SUB-HOSTED-STD"; unit_of_measure: "month"; quantity: 1; unit_price: 8,000; start_date: 2027-05-15; end_date: 2028-05-14; gl_code: 5400; cost_center: CIRRUS-SVC
> 2) description: "Onboarding credit (one-time)"; sku_or_task_id: "CREDIT-ONB"; unit_of_measure: "each"; quantity: 1; unit_price: -2000; gl_code: 5410
> 
> Example B — SOW / Professional Services: 
> 1) description: "Integration implementation — discovery"; sku_or_task_id: "PS-DISC"; unit_of_measure: "day"; quantity: 3; unit_price: 1,200; gl_code: 5500
> 2) description: "Integration implementation — delivery"; sku_or_task_id: "PS-DEL"; unit_of_measure: "day"; quantity: 5; unit_price: 1,200; gl_code: 5500
> 
> Notes: keep the billing granularity consistent with the SOW — this avoids rework when AP ingests invoices. If you use an external SOW doc, include the SOW id in sku_or_task_id so we can reconcile automatically.

If you want, we can pre-populate the CSV with the two examples above once you confirm product vs services split.
